title: Influence of Vitamin C Supplementation on Oxidative Stress and Neutrophil Inflammatory Response in Acute and Regular Exercise
authors: Ljiljana M. Popovic, Nebojsa R. Mitic, Dijana Miric, Boban Bisevac, Mirjana Miric, Brankica Popovic
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C's impact on oxidative stress and neutrophil inflammation from exercise. Vitamin C supplementation reduced exercise-induced lipid peroxidation but did not affect neutrophil inflammatory response.

title: Does Vitamin C and E Supplementation Impair the Favorable Adaptations of Regular Exercise?
authors: Michalis G. Nikolaidis, Chad M. Kerksick, Manfred Lamprecht, Steven R. McAnulty
abstract: This study investigated whether vitamin C and E supplementation interferes with exercise adaptations. High doses of these vitamins are not recommended for exercising individuals due to conflicting evidence on their efficacy and potential harm.

title: Can supplementation with vitamin C and E alter physiological adaptations to strength training?
authors: Gøran Paulsen, Kristoffer T Cumming, Håvard Hamarsland, Elisabet Børsheim, Sveinung Berntsen, Truls ...
source: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
abstract: High doses of vitamins C and E were tested for their effects on strength training adaptations in young and older men. Supplementation blunted adaptations in young men but showed potential benefits in older men.

title: Differences in the Pro/Antioxidative Status and Cellular Stress Response in Elderly Women after 6 Weeks of Exercise Training Supported by 1000 mg of Vitamin C Supplementation
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Ewa Sadowska-Krępa, Elisabetta Damiani, Luca Tiano, Ewa Ziemann, Alicja Nowak-...
abstract: This study examined the effects of exercise training with vitamin C supplementation on antioxidant status and cellular stress response in elderly women. Vitamin C supplementation increased oxidative stress markers and influenced minor changes in gene expression related to training adaptation.

title: Vitamin C and E Supplementation Effects in Professional Soccer Players Under Regular Training
authors: Claudio C Zoppi, Rodrigo Hohl, Fernando C Silva, Fernanda L Lazarim, Joaquim MF Antunes Neto, Mirtes...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C and E supplementation in professional soccer players during training. Supplementation reduced lipid peroxidation and muscle damage but did not improve performance.

title: Exercise Training and Vitamin C Supplementation Affects Ferritin mRNA in Leukocytes without Affecting Prooxidative/Antioxidative Balance in Elderly Women
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Agata Grzybkowska, Monika Wiech, Robert Urbański, Wanda Pilch, Anna Piotrowska...
abstract: Exercise training with vitamin C supplementation decreased ferritin mRNA in elderly women's leukocytes. This intervention did not alter the prooxidative/antioxidative balance.

title: Effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on endogenous antioxidant systems and heat shock proteins in response to endurance training
authors: Kristoffer T. Cumming, Truls Raastad, Geir Holden, Nasser E. Bastani, Damaris Schneeberger, Maria Pa...
abstract: This study examined vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on antioxidant and heat shock protein systems during endurance training. Supplementation did not alter long-term training adaptations but increased acute exercise stress responses.

title: Effects of Acute Vitamin C plus Vitamin E Supplementation on Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage in Runners: A Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: María Martínez-Ferrán, Víctor Cuadrado-Peñafiel, Juan Manuel Sánchez-Andreo, Marta Villar-Lucas, Món...
abstract: This study investigated if vitamin C and E supplementation reduces exercise-induced muscle damage in runners. The supplementation did not significantly improve muscle damage markers or performance compared to a placebo.

title: Vitamin C and E supplementation does not affect heat shock proteins or endogenous antioxidants in trained skeletal muscles during 12 weeks of strength training
authors: K. T. Cumming, T. Raastad, A. Sørstrøm, M. P. Paronetto, N. Mercatelli, I. Ugelstad, D. Caporossi, G...
abstract: This study examined the impact of vitamin C and E supplementation on trained individuals undergoing strength training. The supplementation did not alter acute exercise stress responses or long-term adaptations in heat shock proteins or endogenous antioxidants.

title: Can vitamin C supplementation reverse the effects of exercise training in polluted air on oxidative stress markers? A randomized controlled trial
authors: Amin Eatemadyboroujeni, Mehdi Kargarfard, Hojatollah Alaei
abstract: This study investigated the effects of exercise, polluted air, and vitamin C on oxidative stress markers in rats. Vitamin C supplementation did not significantly reverse the increased oxidative stress caused by exercise in polluted air.

title: The Effect of Vitamin C and E Supplementation on Muscle Damage and Oxidative Stress in Female Athletes: A Clinical Trial
authors: Maryam Taghiyar, Leila Darvishi, Gholamrez Askari, Awat Feizi, Mitra Hariri, Nafiseh Shokri Mashhadi...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on muscle damage and oxidative stress in female athletes. Results showed vitamin C and E supplementation reduced muscle damage and oxidative stress markers.

title: The effects of antioxidant vitamin supplementation on resistance exercise induced lipid peroxidation in trained and untrained participants
authors: Peter E Viitala, Ian J Newhouse, Norm LaVoie, Christine Gottardo
abstract: This study investigated the impact of vitamin E supplementation on exercise-induced lipid peroxidation in trained and untrained individuals. Vitamin E supplementation did not reduce oxidative damage, and training status did not affect lipid peroxidation levels post-exercise.

title: Effect of six weeks 1000 mg/day vitamin C supplementation and healthy training in elderly women on genes expression associated with the immune response - a randomized controlled trial
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Agata Grzybkowska, Mariusz Zasada, Anna Piotrowska, Danuta Dworakowska, Olga C...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study examined the effect of vitamin C supplementation and exercise on immune gene expression in elderly women. While most genes showed no significant change, vitamin C supplementation showed a tendency to alter IL-6 and IL-10 expression.

title: Controversies of antioxidant vitamins supplementation in exercise: ergogenic or ergolytic effects in humans?
authors: Cainara Lins Draeger, Andréia Naves, Natália Marques, Ana Beatriz Baptistella, Renata Alves Carnauba...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This commentary reviews recent studies on antioxidant vitamin supplementation and exercise-induced oxidative stress. Findings are controversial, with supplementation showing ergogenic, ergolytic, or no effects on physiological parameters and antioxidant enzyme activity.

title: Vitamin C may alleviate exercise-induced bronchoconstriction: a meta-analysis
authors: Harri Hemilä
abstract: This meta-analysis examined if vitamin C affects exercise-induced bronchoconstriction. Vitamin C administration significantly reduced post-exercise FEV1 decline and the proportion of participants experiencing EIB.

title: Elevated hepcidin serum level in response to inflammatory and iron signals in exercising athletes is independent of moderate supplementation with vitamin C and E
authors: Víctor Díaz, Ana B Peinado, Laura Barba-Moreno, Sandro Altamura, Javier Butragueño, Marcela González...
abstract: This study investigated hepcidin levels in athletes after exercise. Hepcidin remained elevated despite vitamin C and E supplementation, indicating these vitamins do not alter the response to inflammatory and iron signals.

title: Vitamin C and E supplementation and high intensity interval training induced changes in lipid profile and haematological variables of young males
authors: Surojit Sarkar, Swapan Kr Dey, Gouriprosad Datta, Amit Bandyopadhyay
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on high-intensity interval training (HIIT) in young males. Supplementation protected against negative hematological changes and improved lipid profiles and explosive strength without affecting endurance.

title: The Effect of Vitamins C and E Supplementation on Muscle Damage, Performance, and Body Composition in Athlete Women: A Clinical Trial
authors: Maryam Taghiyar, Reza Ghiasvand, Gholamreza Askari, Awat Feizi, Mitra Hariri, Nafiseh Shokri Mashhad...
abstract: This clinical trial examined the effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on muscle damage, performance, and body composition in trained female athletes over four weeks. The study found no significant improvements in any of these parameters due to the supplementation.

title: Effects of Vitamin C Supplementation on Plasma and Urinary Vitamin C Concentration in Korean Women
authors: Jayoung Choi, Do-Yeon Kim, Ryowon Choue, Hyunjung Lim
abstract: This study investigated the effects of 100 mg and 2,000 mg vitamin C supplements on Korean women. Both doses increased plasma and urinary vitamin C, with the higher dose reducing oxidative stress and the lower dose reducing fatigue.

title: Vitamin C Supplementation Slightly Improves Physical Activity Levels and Reduces Cold Incidence in Men with Marginal Vitamin C Status: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Carol S. Johnston, Gillean M. Barkyoumb, Sara S. Schumacher
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C supplementation's effects on physical activity and colds in men with marginal vitamin C status. Supplementation slightly increased physical activity and reduced cold incidence and duration.

title: Vitamin C, A and E supplementation decreases the expression of  HSPA1A  and  HSPB1  genes in the leukocytes of young polish figure skaters during a 10-day training camp
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Zbigniew Jastrzębski, Grzegorz Chruściński, Monika Michałowska–Sawczyn, Alicja...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study examined the effect of vitamin A, C, and E supplementation on gene expression in young figure skaters during a training camp. Supplementation significantly decreased the expression of stress-related genes HSPA1A and HSPB1 in leukocytes.

title: Comparative effects of vitamin D and vitamin C supplementations with and without endurance physical activity on metabolic syndrome patients: a randomized controlled trial
authors: Halgord Ali M. Farag, Mohammad Javad Hosseinzadeh-Attar, Belal A. Muhammad, Ahmad Esmaillzadeh, Abde...
abstract: This study compared vitamin D and C supplementation with and without exercise in metabolic syndrome patients. Combining supplements with exercise maximized benefits, particularly for vitamin D regarding glucose, cholesterol, and blood pressure.

title: Effect of exercise training on saliva brain derived neurotrophic factor, catalase and vitamin c
authors: Parvin Babaei, Arsalan Damirchi, Bahram Soltani Tehrani, Yazgaldi Nazari, Reyhaneh Sariri, Rastegar ...
source: Medical Journal of the Islamic Republic of Iran
abstract: This study examined salivary antioxidants and BDNF in sedentary men after exhaustive exercise. Acute exercise reduced catalase, vitamin C, and BDNF, with BDNF showing a prolonged decrease.

title: Prior exercise and antioxidant supplementation: effect on oxidative stress and muscle injury
authors: Richard J Bloomer, Michael J Falvo, Brian K Schilling, Webb A Smith
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of prior eccentric exercise and antioxidant supplementation on muscle injury and oxidative stress in resistance-trained men. Neither intervention, alone or combined, significantly reduced markers of muscle injury or oxidative stress.

title: Synergistic Role of Aerobic Exercise and Vitamin C in Reducing Hypertension and Restoring Redox–Inflammatory Balance
authors: Sheraz Ahmad, Khalid Abdul Majeed, Saima Masood, Muhammad Shahbaz Yousaf, Muhammad Bilal Akram, Abdu...
abstract: Aerobic exercise and vitamin C were studied for their effects on hypertension in rats. Combined intervention most effectively lowered blood pressure and improved hypertension-related changes.

title: Marginal Ascorbate Status (Hypovitaminosis C) Results in an Attenuated Response to Vitamin C Supplementation
authors: Anitra C. Carr, Juliet M. Pullar, Stephanie M. Bozonet, Margreet C. M. Vissers
abstract: This study analyzed vitamin C supplementation in individuals with low baseline levels. A 50 mg/day supplement was insufficient to restore adequate vitamin C status in these individuals.

title: Does quercetin and vitamin C improve exercise performance, muscle damage, and body composition in male athletes?
authors: Gholamreza Askari, Reza Ghiasvand, Jahangir Karimian, Awat Feizi, Zamzam Paknahad, Gholamreza Sharif...
source: Journal of Research in Medical Sciences : The Official Journal of Isfahan University of Medical Sciences
abstract: This study investigated the effects of quercetin and vitamin C supplementation on male athletes' exercise performance, muscle damage, and body composition. The supplementation did not improve exercise performance but reduced muscle damage and body fat percentage.

title: Vitamin C and E Treatment Blocks Changes in Kynurenine Metabolism Triggered by Three Weeks of Sprint Interval Training in Recreationally Active Elderly Humans
authors: Victoria L. Wyckelsma, Ada Trepci, Lilly Schwieler, Tomas Venckunas, Marius Brazaitis, Sigitas Kaman...
abstract: Sprint interval training in elderly men altered kynurenine pathway metabolism towards neuroprotection. This beneficial shift was prevented by concurrent vitamin C and E supplementation.

title: Antioxidant Supplementation Hinders the Role of Exercise Training as a Natural Activator of SIRT1
authors: Carmine Sellitto, Graziamaria Corbi, Berenice Stefanelli, Valentina Manzo, Marta Trucillo, Bruno Cha...
abstract: Exercise training increases SIRT1 levels, which boosts the body's antioxidant system. However, antioxidant supplements appear to interfere with this exercise-induced activation of SIRT1.

title: Marginal vitamin C status is associated with reduced fat oxidation during submaximal exercise in young adults
authors: Carol S Johnston, Corinne Corte, Pamela D Swan
abstract: Marginal vitamin C status was studied in relation to fat oxidation during submaximal exercise. Low vitamin C status was associated with reduced fat oxidation, which was improved by vitamin C repletion.

title: Effects of ascorbic acid supplementation on oxidative stress markers in healthy women following a single bout of exercise
authors: Manita Yimcharoen, Suwatsin Kittikunnathum, Chawannut Suknikorn, Wichuda Nak-on, Petcharee Yeethong,...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated ascorbic acid's effects on oxidative stress markers in women after exercise. Ascorbic acid improved antioxidant capacity but did not prevent exercise-induced muscle damage.

title: Elastic resistance training is more effective than vitamin D3 supplementation in reducing oxidative stress and strengthen antioxidant enzymes in healthy men
authors: Fardin Kalvandi, Mohammad Ali Azarbayjani, Ronak Azizbeigi, Kamal Azizbeigi
abstract: Elastic resistance training was studied with and without vitamin D3 supplementation in healthy men. Elastic resistance training alone was more effective than with vitamin D3 supplementation for reducing oxidative stress and strengthening antioxidant enzymes.

title: Vitamin C‐Dependent Intergenerational Inheritance of Enhanced Endurance Performance Following Maternal Exercise
authors: Haiwang Shi, Jie Li, Fan Li, Haoyang Yu, Fulong Zhang, Tao Wu, Luodan Yang, Yuecheng Li, Rui Hu, Men...
abstract: Maternal exercise enhances offspring endurance through muscle and mitochondrial changes, with benefits inherited across generations. This effect is mediated by vitamin C's role in regulating DNA methylation via the TET2-SVCT2 pathway.

title: The interaction effects of aerobic exercise training and vitamin D supplementation on plasma lipid profiles and insulin resistance in ovariectomized rats
authors: Parvin Babaei, Arsalan Damirchi, Rastegar Hoseini
abstract: This study investigated the combined effects of aerobic exercise and vitamin D on ovariectomized rats. The combination significantly improved lipid profiles and reduced insulin resistance.

title: The effect of combined resistance exercise training and vitamin D 3  supplementation on musculoskeletal health and function in older adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Anneka Elizabeth Antoniak, Carolyn A Greig
abstract: This systematic review evaluated combined resistance exercise and vitamin D supplementation in older adults. The combination significantly improved lower limb muscle strength compared to exercise alone.

title: Nordic Walking Training Causes a Decrease in Blood Cholesterol in Elderly Women Supplemented with Vitamin D
authors: Krzysztof Prusik, Jakub Kortas, Katarzyna Prusik, Jan Mieszkowski, Joanna Jaworska, Wojciech Skrobot...
abstract: Nordic Walking training combined with vitamin D supplementation was studied in elderly women. This intervention significantly decreased total cholesterol, LDL-C, and triglycerides.

title: Vitamin C and E Treatment Blunts Sprint Interval Training–Induced Changes in Inflammatory Mediator-, Calcium-, and Mitochondria-Related Signaling in Recreationally Active Elderly Humans
authors: Victoria L. Wyckelsma, Tomas Venckunas, Marius Brazaitis, Stefano Gastaldello, Audrius Snieckus, Ner...
abstract: Sprint interval training in elderly individuals was studied with and without antioxidant treatment. Antioxidants blunted training-induced cellular signaling changes in muscle, but did not affect performance outcomes.

title: Effects of vitamin D supplementation and circuit training on indices of obesity and insulin resistance in T2D and vitamin D deficient elderly women
authors: Hyoung-Jun Kim, Chang-Kyun Kang, Hyon Park, Man-Gyoon Lee
abstract: This study examined the effects of vitamin D and circuit training on obese, vitamin D-deficient elderly women with type 2 diabetes. Circuit training alone improved body composition, abdominal fat, and blood lipids, while combined treatment showed a trend toward improved insulin resistance.

title: The effect of aquatic training and vitamin D3 supplementation on bone metabolism in postmenopausal obese women
authors: Foroozandeh Zaravar, Gholamhossein Tamaddon, Leila Zaravar, Maryam Koushkie Jahromi
source: Journal of Exercise Science and Fitness
abstract: This study investigated the effects of aquatic training and vitamin D3 supplementation on bone metabolism in postmenopausal obese women. Combining both interventions was most effective for improving bone metabolism, while vitamin D alone was insufficient and aquatic training did not improve vitamin D levels.

title: Short-Term High-Dose Vitamin C and E Supplementation Attenuates Muscle Damage and Inflammatory Responses to Repeated Taekwondo Competitions: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial
authors: Chun-Chung Chou, Yu-Chi Sung, Glen Davison, Chung-Yu Chen, Yi-Hung Liao
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on elite Taekwondo athletes. Supplementation attenuated muscle damage, hemolysis, and inflammatory responses to repeated competitions.

title: Combined effects of vitamin D supplementation and endurance exercise training on insulin resistance in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus patients with vitamin D deficiency: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial
authors: Mi Xiang, Xiaomin Sun, Junxiang Wei, Zhen-Bo Cao
abstract: This study protocol outlines a randomized controlled trial investigating the combined effects of vitamin D and endurance exercise on insulin resistance in newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes patients. The research aims to determine if this combination offers synergistic benefits beyond individual interventions.

title: Combined effect of antioxidant supplementation and resistance training on oxidative stress markers, muscle and body composition in an elderly population
authors: F. Bobeuf; M. Labonte; I.J. Dionne; Abdelouahed Khalil
source: The Journal of Nutrition, Health & Aging
abstract: This study was aimed to examine the effect of vitamin C/E intake alone or combined with resistance training on antioxidant/pro-oxidant status, muscle strength and body composition in an elderly popula

title: Cashew apple juice supplementation enhanced fat utilization during high-intensity exercise in trained and untrained men
authors: Piyapong Prasertsri, Thapanee Roengrit, Yupaporn Kanpetta, Terdthai Tong-un, Supaporn Muchimapura, J...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: Cashew apple juice supplementation was studied for its effect on substrate utilization during high-intensity exercise. CAJ supplementation increased fat oxidation and decreased carbohydrate oxidation during exercise in both trained and untrained men.

title: Effects of vitamins C and E supplementation combined with 12-week resistance training in older women with sarcopenia: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
authors: Xu Liu, Bo Chen, Yutian Jin, Feiyan Zhong, Yunjuan Zhang, Yu Li, Yun Zhang, Runhong Cui, Bing Wu, Cu...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of combined vitamin C, E, and resistance training in older women with sarcopenia. Supplementation with vitamins C and E enhanced muscle mass and strength gains compared to placebo.

title: A Comparison of the Antioxidant Effects Between Hydrogen Gas Inhalation and Vitamin C Supplementation in Response to a 60-Min Treadmill Exercise in Rat Gastrocnemius Muscle
authors: Li Chaoqun, Zhao Yuqi, Zhou Shi, Yu Zhenghui, Wen Li
abstract: Hydrogen gas inhalation and vitamin C were compared for their antioxidant effects on rat gastrocnemius muscle after treadmill exercise. Hydrogen gas reduced oxidative stress without blunting mitochondrial biogenesis signals, unlike vitamin C.

title: Efficacy of Vitamin D Supplementation in Addition to Aerobic Exercise Training in Obese Women with Perceived Myalgia: A Single-Blinded Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial
authors: Heba Ahmed Ali Abdeen, David Rodriguez-Sanz, Mahmoud Ewidea, Dina Mohamed Ali Al-Hamaky, Marwa Abd E...
abstract: This study examined vitamin D and aerobic exercise for obese women with muscle pain. Combining both treatments was most effective for reducing pain, improving vitamin D levels, and enhancing quality of life.

title: Effect of an 8-weeks aerobic training program in elderly on oxidative stress and Hsp72 expression in leukocytes during antioxidant supplementation
authors: David Simar; D. Malatesta; E. Mas; M. Delage; C. Caillaud
source: The Journal of Nutrition, Health & Aging
abstract: To investigate the effect of aerobic training in the context of antioxidant supplementation on systemic oxidative stress and leukocytes heat shock protein (Hsp)72 expression in the elderly. Sixteen se

title: The effects of exercise training and acute exercise duration on plasma folate and vitamin B 12
authors: Young-Nam Kim, Ji Hyeon Hwang, Youn-Ok Cho
abstract: This study examined how exercise training and acute exercise duration affect plasma folate and vitamin B12 in rats. Regular exercise training lowered folate and raised vitamin B12, but acute exercise duration had no significant impact on these vitamins.

title: Influence of combined vitamin D 3  supplementation and resistance exercise training on musculoskeletal health in older men and women (EXVITD): protocol for a randomised controlled trial
authors: Anneka Elizabeth Welford, Susan Lanham-New, Janet Lord, Alison Doyle, Julie Robinson, Peter Nighting...
abstract: This randomized controlled trial investigates the effect of vitamin D3 supplementation combined with resistance exercise training on musculoskeletal health in older adults. The study aims to determine if this combination improves muscle function more than exercise training alone.

title: Effects of Exercise Alone or Combined With Cognitive Training and Vitamin D Supplementation to Improve Cognition in Adults With Mild Cognitive Impairment
authors: Manuel Montero-Odasso, Guangyong Zou, Mark Speechley, Quincy J. Almeida, Teresa Liu-Ambrose, Laura E...
abstract: A 20-week multidomain intervention combining exercise and cognitive training improved cognition in adults with mild cognitive impairment. Adding vitamin D did not enhance these cognitive benefits.

title: Synergistic Effects of Exercise Training and Vitamin D Supplementation on Mitochondrial Function of Cardiac Tissue, Antioxidant Capacity, and Tumor Growth in Breast Cancer in Bearing-4T1 Mice
authors: Ali Jafari, Dariush Sheikholeslami-Vatani, Farnoosh Khosrobakhsh, Neda Khaledi
abstract: This study examined the effects of exercise and vitamin D on breast cancer mice. Combining exercise and vitamin D inhibited tumor growth, improved antioxidant capacity, and positively modulated cardiac gene expression.

title: Effects of Dietary Vitamin C Supplementation on Vitamin C Synthesis, Transport, and Egg Deposition in Breeding Geese
authors: Yanglei Hu, Rong Xu, Yating Zhou, Ning Li, Haiming Yang, Jian Wang, Hongchang Zhao, Jun Yu
source: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI
abstract: This study investigated the impact of dietary vitamin C on vitamin C levels and transport in breeding geese. Supplementation increased vitamin C in egg yolks and serum by enhancing intestinal absorption and yolk deposition, while suppressing synthesis.

title: Influence of Vitamin D Supplementation by Sunlight or Oral D3 on Exercise Performance
authors: ALEXANDER T. CARSWELL, SAMUEL J. OLIVER, LAUREL M. WENTZ, DANIEL S. KASHI, ROSS ROBERTS, JONATHAN C....
source: Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise
abstract: A prospective study found vitamin D status positively correlated with endurance, but not strength or power. Supplementing to achieve vitamin D sufficiency via sunlight or oral D3 did not improve exercise performance.

title: Acute vitamin C improves cardiac function, not exercise capacity, in adults with type 2 diabetes
authors: Rebecca L. Scalzo, Timothy A. Bauer, Kylie Harrall, Kerrie Moreau, Cemal Ozemek, Leah Herlache, Shaw...
abstract: Acute vitamin C infusion was studied in adults with type 2 diabetes and healthy adults. Vitamin C improved diastolic cardiac function but did not affect exercise capacity or other measures of vascular function.

title: Anti-Inflammatory Effects of a Period of Aerobic Training and Vitamin D Supplementation in Postmenopausal Women with Metabolic Syndrome
authors: Parivash Najafi Nazarabadi, Zaher Etemad, Rastegar Hoseini, Fatah Moradi
abstract: This study examined the anti-inflammatory effects of aerobic training and vitamin D supplementation in postmenopausal women with metabolic syndrome. The combination of exercise and vitamin D significantly reduced inflammatory markers and improved metabolic syndrome indices more than either intervention alone.

title: Antioxidant Supplementation Impairs Changes in Body Composition Induced by Strength Training in Young Women
authors: MAURILIO T. DUTRA, SÁVIO ALEX, ALYSON F. SILVA, LEE E. BROWN, MARTIM BOTTARO
abstract: This study examined the effects of strength training with antioxidant supplementation on body composition in young women. Antioxidant supplementation impaired strength training-induced gains in fat-free mass and reductions in fat mass.

title: Effects of branched-chain amino acid- and vitamin D-containing high-protein food supplementation plus exercise on elderly people with decreased physical functions
authors: Yoshihiro Nakamura, Takuji Yokoe, Koki Ouchi, Taro Funamoto, Hiroyuki Kimura, Koichiro Hamada, Hidek...
abstract: This study examined the effects of exercise plus a high-protein food supplement containing BCAAs and vitamin D on elderly individuals with decreased physical function. The combination of exercise and supplementation prevented declines in soft lean mass and improved physical performance compared to exercise alone or no intervention.

title: Protective Role of Vitamin C Intake on Muscle Damage in Male Adolescents Performing Strenuous Physical Activity
authors: Shreef G. N. Gabrial, Marie-Christine R. Shakib, Gamal N. Gabrial
source: Open Access Macedonian Journal of Medical Sciences
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C's effect on muscle damage in male adolescents during strenuous exercise. Vitamin C supplementation significantly reduced markers of muscle damage, oxidative stress, and inflammation.

title: High Baseline Vitamin C Levels Do Not Prevent a Positive Outcome of a Lifestyle Intervention
authors: Matthias Blüher, Michael Stumvoll, C. Ronald Kahn, Michael Ristow

title: Impact of exercise training and supplemental oxygen on submaximal exercise performance in patients with COPD
authors: Daniel Neunhäuserer, Bernhard Reich, Barbara Mayr, Bernhard Kaiser, Bernd Lamprecht, David Niedersee...
source: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
abstract: This study examined the effects of exercise training with and without supplemental oxygen on COPD patients' submaximal exercise performance. Exercise training improved exercise tolerance and capacity, with supplemental oxygen having minimal additional benefits.

title: Effects of vitamin D supplementation combined with exercise on glucolipid metabolism in adults: A meta-analysis
authors: Yue Feng, Wenxing Zhou, Yanjun Niu
abstract: This meta-analysis evaluated the effects of vitamin D and exercise combined on glucolipid metabolism. The combination significantly improved blood glucose, fasting insulin, and insulin resistance, and increased vitamin D levels.

title: Vitamin A Oral Supplementation Induces Oxidative Stress and Suppresses IL-10 and HSP70 in Skeletal Muscle of Trained Rats
authors: Lyvia Lintzmaier Petiz, Carolina Saibro Girardi, Rafael Calixto Bortolin, Alice Kunzler, Juciano Gas...
abstract: Vitamin A supplementation was studied in trained rats. It impaired exercise-induced antioxidant capacity and suppressed anti-inflammatory responses in skeletal muscle.

title: Enhancing Supplemental Effects of Acute Natural Antioxidant Derived from Yeast Fermentation and Vitamin C on Sports Performance in Triathlon Athletes: A Randomized, Double-Blinded, Placebo-Controlled, Crossover Trial
authors: Eunjoo Lee, Hun-Young Park, Sung-Woo Kim, Yerin Sun, Jae-Ho Choi, Jisoo Seo, Yanghoon Peter Jung, Ah...
abstract: This study examined the effects of combined vitamin C and glutathione supplementation on middle-aged triathletes during exercise. The combination improved metabolic, skeletal muscle oxygenation, cardiac, and antioxidant functions compared to individual supplements or placebo.

title: Effects of aerobic training and vitamin D supplementation on glycemic indices and adipose tissue gene expression in type 2 diabetic rats
authors: Kimya Khaledi, Rastegar Hoseini, Ahmad Gharzi
abstract: Aerobic training and vitamin D supplementation were studied in type 2 diabetic rats. Combined intervention significantly upregulated key genes in visceral adipose tissue compared to individual treatments.

title: Regular sling core stabilization training improves bone density based on calcium and vitamin D supplementation
authors: Jing Liu, Daoming Xu, Lanying Liu, Chihuan Huang, Zhijie Guo, Di Zhang, Liyu Wei
abstract: This paper reports on a case study of a 70-year-old woman with osteoporosis. Regular sling core stabilization training, combined with calcium and vitamin D supplementation, improved her bone density and relieved back pain.

title: Antioxidant Vitamin C Prevents Decline in Endothelial Function during Sitting
authors: Saurabh S. Thosar, Sylvanna L. Bielko, Chad S. Wiggins, James E. Klaunig, Kieren J. Mather, Janet P....
source: Medical Science Monitor : International Medical Journal of Experimental and Clinical Research
abstract: This study investigated if Vitamin C prevents endothelial function decline during prolonged sitting. Vitamin C supplementation prevented the impairment of femoral artery dilation after three hours of sitting.

title: Exercise May Ameliorate the Detrimental Side Effects of High Vitamin D Supplementation on Muscle Function in Mice
authors: Danielle A Debruin, Cara A Timpani, Hannah Lalunio, Emma Rybalka, Craig A Goodman, Alan Hayes
source: Journal of Bone and Mineral Research
abstract: High vitamin D supplementation reduced muscle force in sedentary mice. Exercise normalized this effect and improved fatigue resistance.

title: Oligomerized lychee fruit extract (OLFE) and a mixture of vitamin C and vitamin E for endurance capacity in a double blind randomized controlled trial
authors: Seung Wan Kang, Seokyung Hahn, Jung-Kyu Kim, Seung-Min Yang, Byung-Joo Park, Sang Chul Lee
source: Journal of Clinical Biochemistry and Nutrition
abstract: Oligomerized lychee fruit extract (OLFE) and a vitamin C/E mixture were tested for endurance effects in exercising males. OLFE significantly improved running time and anaerobic threshold, while the vitamin mixture unexpectedly reduced VO2 max.

title: Combined Effects of Exercise Training and Nutritional Supplementation in Cancer Patients in the Context of the COVID-19: A Perspective Study
authors: Mahdieh Molanouri Shamsi, Alieh Vahed, AmirHossin Ahmadi Hekmatikar, Katsuhiko Suzuki
abstract: This perspective study examines how exercise and nutritional supplements might affect cancer patients' COVID-19 risk. Combining these interventions could boost immune responses against COVID-19 and potentially improve vaccine efficacy.

title: Oral vitamin C supplementation to patients with myeloid cancer on azacitidine treatment: Normalization of plasma vitamin C induces epigenetic changes
authors: Linn Gillberg, Andreas D. Ørskov, Ammar Nasif, Hitoshi Ohtani, Zachary Madaj, Jakob W. Hansen, Nicol...
abstract: This study investigated oral vitamin C supplementation in myeloid cancer patients treated with azacitidine. Normalizing plasma vitamin C levels increased the 5hmC/5mC ratio, suggesting enhanced DNMTi effects.

title: Modification of the Effect of Vitamin E Supplementation on the Mortality of Male Smokers by Age and Dietary Vitamin C
authors: Harri Hemilä, Jaakko Kaprio
abstract: Vitamin E supplementation's effect on mortality in male smokers was examined. Its impact varied significantly by age and dietary vitamin C intake, suggesting heterogeneous effects in different population subgroups.

title: Vitamin D3 supplementation enhances the effect of aerobic water-based training on physical fitness indices in obese and overweight menopausal women: A randomized controlled trial
authors: Foroozandeh Zaravar, Golamhossein Tamaddon, Mohammadamin Safari, Leila Zaravar, Maryam Koushkie Jahr...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of water-based aerobic training and vitamin D3 supplementation on overweight/obese postmenopausal women. Combining both interventions significantly improved BMI, handgrip strength, and gait speed more than either alone.

title: Concurrent effects of high-intensity interval training and vitamin D supplementation on bone metabolism among women diagnosed with osteoporosis: a randomized controlled trial
authors: Ahmad H. Alghadir, Sami A. Gabr, Amir Iqbal
abstract: This study examined the effects of 16 weeks of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and vitamin D supplementation on bone metabolism in women with osteoporosis. Concurrent HIIT and vitamin D supplementation significantly improved bone mineral density and bone metabolism markers more than either intervention alone.

title: Oral vitamin C restores endothelial function during acute inflammation in young and older adults
authors: Elizabeth C. Lefferts, Brooks A. Hibner, Wesley K. Lefferts, Natalia S. Lima, Tracy Baynard, Jacob M...
abstract: Oral vitamin C was given to young and older adults during acute inflammation to assess its effect on vascular function. Vitamin C restored endothelial function, but not aortic stiffness, during inflammation.

title: Antioxidants and Exercise: A Redox-Informed Framework for Training Adaptation, Performance, and Recovery
authors: Dan Cristian Mănescu; Andrei Tudor; Andreea Maria Mănescu; Iulius Radulian Mărgărit; Cătălin Octavia...
abstract: Antioxidants can hinder training adaptations by blunting exercise-induced signals. However, certain food-derived antioxidants may aid recovery without impairing gains. A framework called Redox-Adaptive Periodization is proposed to optimize antioxidant use based on training goals.

title: Exhaustive exercise and vitamins C and E modulate thyroid hormone levels at low and high altitudes
authors: Fahaid Al-Hashem, Mahmoud Alkhateeb, Bahjat Al-Ani, Hussein Sakr, Mohammad Khalil
abstract: Exhaustive exercise and vitamin C/E supplementation were studied in rats at low and high altitudes. The study found that exercise and antioxidants increased thyroid hormones, with reduced T4 to T3 conversion.

title: Effects of vitamin D 3  supplementation on oxidative stress and antioxidant enzyme after strenuous endurance exercise in healthy young men: a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
authors: Cheng-Tse Yang, Pei-Wei Weng, Li-Hui Chien, Sunil Kumar, Ming-Ta Yang
abstract: This study investigated vitamin D3 supplementation's effects on oxidative stress after endurance exercise. Vitamin D3 supplementation mitigated exercise-induced oxidative stress markers in healthy young men.

title: Enhanced Human Neutrophil Vitamin C Status, Chemotaxis and Oxidant Generation Following Dietary Supplementation with Vitamin C-Rich  SunGold  Kiwifruit
authors: Stephanie M. Bozonet, Anitra C. Carr, Juliet M. Pullar, Margreet C. M. Vissers
abstract: Dietary supplementation with vitamin C-rich kiwifruit was studied in men with suboptimal vitamin C status. Supplementation improved neutrophil chemotaxis and oxidant generation, suggesting enhanced immunity.

title: Exercise performance and physiological responses: the potential role of redox imbalance
authors: Kavey Vidal, Nathaniel Robinson, Stephen J. Ives
abstract: This study investigated the effects of hyperoxia and an antioxidant cocktail on cycling performance and physiological responses. Ingesting an antioxidant cocktail impaired performance, ventilation, and economy, suggesting a disruption of redox balance.

title: EFFECTS OF L-ASCORBIC ACID AND ALPHA-TOCOPHEROL ON BIOCHEMICAL PARAMETERS OF SWIMMING-INDUCED OXIDATIVE STRESS IN SERUM OF GUINEA PIGS
authors: Marija Bursać-Mitrović, Dragan R. Milovanović, Radoslav Mitić, Danijela Jovanović, Miroslav Sovrlić,...
source: African Journal of Traditional, Complementary, and Alternative Medicines
abstract: This study investigated the effects of L-ascorbic acid and alpha-tocopherol on biochemical markers of oxidative stress in guinea pigs after swimming. The vitamins demonstrated protective antioxidant activity, with combined treatments showing a synergistic effect.

title: Supplemental Oxygen during Exercise Training in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
authors: SARA FAGGIAN, FRANCESCA BATTISTA, MARCO VECCHIATO, RICHARD CASABURI, MARGARETA EMTNER, NICOLA BORASI...
source: Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise
abstract: This review examines supplemental oxygen's role in COPD exercise training. Supplemental oxygen may benefit specific patients and conditions, particularly with high-intensity training, to enhance exercise tolerance and adaptations.

title: Human skeletal muscle ascorbate is highly responsive to changes in vitamin C intake and plasma concentrations 1 2 3
authors: Anitra C Carr, Stephanie M Bozonet, Juliet M Pullar, Jeremy W Simcock, Margreet CM Vissers
abstract: Skeletal muscle ascorbate levels were studied in response to vitamin C intake from kiwifruit. Muscle ascorbate concentrations significantly increased with intake and were more responsive than leukocytes.

title: Effects of exercise training and dietary supplement on fat free mass and bone mass density during weight loss – a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Anja Roth, Martin Sattelmayer, Chloé Schorderet, Simone Gafner, Lara Allet, Nahid Ramezani-Jolfaie, ...
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined exercise training and dietary supplements' effects on fat-free mass during weight loss. Exercise training, particularly combined with high protein intake, significantly helps preserve fat-free mass.

title: Effects of High-Dose Vitamin D Supplementation and Physical Exercise on Vitamin D Metabolites in Professional Football Players: A Pilot Study
authors: Anna Książek, Aleksandra Zagrodna, Konrad Kowalski
abstract: This pilot study examined vitamin D metabolite changes in professional football players during and after exercise, with and without high-dose supplementation. Physical activity increased vitamin D metabolites, and supplementation further amplified these levels, suggesting rapid status improvement.
